Title: Can I cancel my subscription?
Content: You can cancel your trial or paid subscription through the Subscription section of your account page. Even if you cancel immediately after starting the free trial and regular subscription, you can still use the CLO program until the expiration date. *Please note cancelation of the subscription after the renewal is non-refundable. *Deactivation (remote logout) doesn't cancel your subscription. Step 1. Sign in to your account via clo3d.com Step 2. Navigate to your Subscription page and click the "Cancel Subscription" button. Step 3. Proceed with the survey for the cancelation reason and click the confirmation button. Step 4. Check the Billing section that your subscription expiration date. Please submit an inquiry through our Contact Us page if you have any questions or difficulties.

Title: Does CLO offer student discounts?
Content: Yes, we offer a 50% discount on an Individual plan to eligible high school, college, and university students worldwide. Discounted price will be $25 USD/month or $225 USD/year. Important Note: To receive the student discount, you must verify your student status before starting your trial. If you fail to do so, you will not be eligible for the discount. Student Eligibility To qualify for a student discount, you must be at least 13 years old and enrolled in one of the following: University or college - full-time students in an accredited university or college that offers degrees. Primary or secondary school - full-time students in an accredited primary or secondary school. Im eligible. How can I get the student discount? Please check if your student email is already approved with CLO: Student Eligibility Check When your school domain is already approved, Add your student email. The USE EMAIL ADDRESS button will be activated. Click on the button and create your account. Your account will be automatically applied to the student discount. (You can see the discounted price on your checkout page after the subscription button.) If your school domain is not approved or you don't have a student email address, Go to the SIGN UP page and select Individual. Create your CLO account using either your student email address (if available) or your personal email address. If using a personal email please provide a letter from your school stating they do not provide students with school email addresses After verifying your account, please Contact Us and submit one of the following documents: School ID card with a valid date. Official enrollment verification statement issued within the last 6 months. Tuition statement for the current year/semester. Our support team will review your documents and apply for the discount if approved. If you already have an account with us, Simply Contact Us and submit your proof of enrollment. *Please note that if you can't use your school email after graduation, you would face an issue with receiving CLO emails such as renewal notifications and any CLO news.

Title: Hi-Res Garment
Content: List of Contents Hi-Res Garment Hi-Res Garment Settings Hi-Res Garment - Improve general quality of the 3D Garment after completion. - Select the Hi-Res Garment tool from the 3D toolbar or navigate to and select Main Menu 3D Garment Hi-Res Garment. Hi-Res Garment Settings - Select the Hi-Res Garment tool from the 3D Toolbar and the Hi-Res Properties window will appear. Garment Particle Distance - Change all Patterns Particle Distance to 5mm. - Modify Tolerance to decide the range of Particle Distance so that only Patterns with corresponding Particle Distance value will be affected. Patterns with Particle Distance value outside of the Tolerance will not be affected. Addl Thickness - Collision - Change all Patterns Addl Thickness Collision to the default value, 1mm. - Modify Tollerance to decide the range of Addl Thickness - Collision so that only Patterns with corresponding Addl Thickness - Collision value will be affected. Patterns with Addl Thickness - Collision value outside of the Tolerance will not be affected. Avatar Skin Offset - Change all Avatars Skin Offset to the default value, 0mm. - Modify Tolerance to decide the range of Skin Offset so that only Patterns with corresponding Skin Offset value will be affected. Patterns with Skin Offset value outside of the Tolerance will not be affected. Simulation Simulation Quality - Change the Simulation preset to the default setting, Complete (Nonlinear). - When fabric items other than the Default Fabric is used to the Patterns, the Complete (Nonlinear) Simulation preset shows more realistically accurate length and wrinkles of the 3D Garment. Since the Simulation speed decreases when the Simulation preset is changed to Complete (Nonlinear), it is advised to change to the respective preset only when improving the 3D Garment quality.

Title: Reset 3D Arrangement (All)
Content: Reset 3D ArrangementAll - Re-arrange 3D Patterns prior to the Simulation. - Use the Reset 3D Arrangement(All) tool when Garments are not properly draped after arranging them in the 3D window. - Select the Reset 3D Arrangement(All) tool from the 3D toolbar. - Or, navigate to the Main Menu and select 3D Garment Reset 3D Arrangement(All). - All Patterns will be re-arranged in the 3D window prior to the Simulation.

Title: Reset 2D Arrangement (All)
Content: Reset 2D ArrangementAll - Re-Arrange 3D Patterns according to the Pattern Arrangement in the 2D window. - Select the Reset 2D ArrangementAll) tool from the 3D toolbar. - Or, navigate to the Main Menu and select 3D Garment Reset 2D Arrangement (All). - All Patterns will be re-arranged in the 3D window reflecting the Pattern Arrangement in the 2D window.

Title: Pleats
Content: Objective Create the desired shape of pleats to Patterns. Location Main Menu 2D Pattern Pleats Pleats 2D Toolbar Pleats Operation Select the tool/menu indicated in Location. Click to create a start point and an endpoint of a reference line of the pleats along Pattern Outlines. A Pattern is divided into two. Click on the side where the pleats will be added. The Pleats window appears. Configure the options and select OK. Pleats Type Select the type of the pleats (Knife, Box, or Accordion). Specification Number of Pleats Decide the number of pleats. Depth Assign the depth of the pleats (the depth of folded pleats). Interval Set the interval between pleats when there are two or more pleats. Create Notch Select where to create Notch (Both, Start, or End). Reverse Direction Reverse the direction where the pleats will be added. Option Assign fold angles to the fold lines. Greater the difference between the angle of Outside Fold and Inside Fold, sharper the folds are. The pleats are created on the Pattern. If there is an Internal Line in the Pattern, it is also moved and rotated along with the Pattern. (ver 6.0) Note: If the segment where pleats to be created is sewn to another Pattern, the pleats will be automatically sewn. If the segment is not sewn, use the Pleats Sewing tool to sew the pleats to the other Pattern.

Title: Fold Arrangement
Content: List of Contents Fold Arrangement Fold Patterns Check Fold Angle Sync Fold Arrangement Angle Fold Arrangement - Fold Patterns based on internal lines and sewing lines in the 3D window. - Select the Fold Arrangement tool from the 3D toolbar. - Or, navigate to the Main Menu and select 3D Garment Fold Arrangement Fold Patterns - To use the Fold Arrangement toolthere must be fiducial lines such as Internal Lines and Sewing Lines on Patterns. - Click on the Internal Line or the Sewing Line which the Pattern will fold base on. - When the Gizmo tool appears, click and drag to fold the Pattern towards the desired direction. Check Fold Angle - The Fold Angle of the selected Internal Line or the Sewing Line will change automatically and will be reflected in the Property Editor. - Fold the Pattern with the Fold Arrangement tool and check the Fold Angle. - To create a crisp fold, adjust the Fold Angle to 0 or 360 as desired. Sync Fold Arrangement Angle_ver4.2.0 - Toggle on or off Sync Fold Arrangement Angle - Navigate to Main Menu Settings User Settings 3D Arragement - Toggle off the Sync Fold Arrangement Angle option. - The Fold Angle is not changed when Pattern is fold with the Fold Arrangement tool.

Title: Configurate Library and Create Blocks
Content: List of Contents Modular Library (CLO 7.2) Group and Category (CLO 7.2) Style (CLO 7.2) Block (CLO 7.2) Modular Creator (CLO 7.2) Save Style (CLO 7.2) Save Block (CLO 7.2) Auto Block Creation ( CLO 2024.1) Modular User Setting (CLO 2024.2) Mix and Match (CLO 2024.2) Notch Sewing (CLO 2024.2) Easily and quickly create different variations through previously saved garment blocks within CLO. Modular Library This is where all of your blocks will be to mix and match different styles and blocks, here you can also create and save groups, categories, styles and blocks. Group and Category Both of these sections are Folder based meaning you can bring in folders from anywhere you have access and also create folders anywhere you have access too. Note: The buttons on the top right are Add (to add in a new Group or Category), List (To switch between a list and icons) and Refresh option. Adding a New Group or Category Click the Add button on the top Right, and then select the folder you want to add. The selected folder will be added as a group. Double-click the added group folder, and click the Add button on the top of the category tab. The Add Category window appears. Enter the category name and click the OK button. The category is added to the selected group. Editing Group or Category Select the folder you want to edit and Right click to see your options Copy the Path Delete Style The style is the what all your blocks will be linked to. It is best to think of the different styles as a type of fit so that all your blocks can easily fit together when mixing and matching different blocks. Note: The name of the group and category that this style is saved in, is at the top left. Adding Style Double-click the category folder in which you want to add a style, and click the Add button on the top of the style tab. Style Section window appears. If there is a garment in the 3D window, the thumbnail for that garment is automatically registered. If you want to register thumbnail manually, select Create New Thumbnail and open the image file. Enter the name of the style and press OK button. Style will be added with the thumbnail and the name. Edit Style Select the Style you want to edit and Right Click The Style Selection pop up will come up again and allow you to change the Thumbnail, and Style Name if you want Delete If there are blocks within this style a Warning pop will come up telling you that the blocks will also be erased and asking if you would still like to proceed. Block These are the different pattern pieces that make up one full style. You can add in multiple patterns for one block, they will be what you will use to mix and create different variations of a style. Adding a Block Section Double click the thumbnail of the style that you want to add block, then click the Add block type on the top right Click the Create Block Section menu. Create New Block Type window appears. After setting the information below, click the OK button. Type Set the block type Tag Enter the block tag. If you need to add 2 or more of the same type, categorize them through tags. When the types and tags are added in the same status, the existing block type will be overwritten the block type is added to the selected style. Adding A Pattern to a block Section Within the Block Section select the Add button A Warning window will pop up if the patterns within the file have not been saved as a style. You can continue to proceed or cancel and save the garment as a style Using the Modular Configurator The Patterns for that block will then be selectable within the 2D window. To select multiple pattern hold down the shift key Once all the pattern are selected hit Enter on your key board The Block Section window will pop up The Block thumbnail will automatically be added based on 3D window If you want to register a thumbnail manually you can select create New Thumbnail The Thumbnail and name will automatically be added to the Block Section in the Modular Library Edit Block Select the Block you want to edit and Right Click The Block Selection pop up will come up again and allow you to change the Thumbnail, and File Name if you want. Delete A Warning pop will come up telling you that this will erase the block for all areas and if you would like to proceed. Modular Configurator This is specifically for saving out style or blocks. This method brings you directly to the Modular Creator which makes saving out styles or blocks a little quicker. Save Style: Select the Group &amp Category to save this style under Can also create a new Group or Category using the add button at the top Select the Add button to add a new Style The Style Section Window will appear If there is a garment in the 3D window, the thumbnail for that garment is automatically registered. If you want to register thumbnail manually, select Create New Thumbnail and open the image file. Enter the name of the style and press OK button. Style will be added with the thumbnail and the name. Save Block Select the Group &amp Category to save this style under Can also create a new Group or Category using the add button at the top Select the Style to save the blocks under Can also create a new style using the add button at the top Add in the Block Type using the Add button at the top Note: Can also use the Auto Modular Labeling tool this will automatically add in all the blocks and assign all patterns to the coinciding blocks Create New Block Type window appears. After setting the information below, click the OK button. Type Set the block type Tag Enter the block tag. If you need to add 2 or more of the same type, categorize them through tags. When the types and tags are added in the same status, the existing block type will be overwritten the block type is added to the selected style. The Patterns for that block will then be selectable within the 2D window. To select multiple pattern hold down the shift key Once all the pattern are selected hit Enter on your key board The Block Section window will pop up The Block thumbnail will automatically be added based on 3D window If you want to register a thumbnail manually you can select create New Thumbnail The Thumbnail and name will automatically be added to the Block Section in the Modular Library Auto Block Creation Auto Modular Labeling is based on the results learned from numerous pattern data and analyzes which part of the pattern it is based on only the shape of the pattern. . This options is possible in both the Modular Library and the Modular Configurator. Once there are block sections within the style the Auto Modular Labeling icon will be active Click the Auto Modular Labeling button at the top right of the Modular Library. The Modular Creator Widow will come up Check all that all patterns are correctly assigned to the right blocks within your 2D window Each pattern is automatically recognized and displayed as the corresponding block. blocks, Click Save Block button to set thumbnail image and file name, then click OK button. The Check mark will then be activated to signal that this block is ready Click the Add button. The Check Sewing tag window appears. After checking whether the block pattern is sewn well with other block patterns, click the OK button. If you need to reset the sewing line, click the Cancel button to correct the sewing line and try again. The selected pattern will be created as a block of that type. Note: Click the Edit Block button if any patterns were not added to a block type or if any pattern was applied incorrectly. Modular User Setting Mix and Match: To protect the users from apply different block fits together turn on the option Prevent Mix and Match When Prevent Mix and Match is active a Warning pop up will appear when a block from one style is being applied to a separate style. Note: Applying blocks from a raglan style, then switching to a set in style and selecting a sleeve this will then cause the warning window to appear. Notch Sewing: To save out a specific sewing relationship activate the Notching Sewing option. The Modular sewing tags will then follow the notch placements for sewing relationships.

Title: POM Object Browser
Content: New in 2024.2 List of Content Folders Add Move Delete View Graded Sizes Improving the POM object browser so users can organize and view they points of measure easily within CLO. Organize Folders Using the folders within POM will allow you to organize all your POM however you like, for example you could organize them by pattern piece, or by measurement type, any way that works for you. Add Click on the Add Folder button at the top in POM tab in Object Browser. Edit the folder name and then click away or hit Enter key to apply the changes. * Afterwards, double-click on the folder name to rename it. Click on the Add button within folder to add new POM within a folder. Click on the Arrow within the Folder to collapse all the POM in the folder. Move Drag and drop the POMs between the different folders to move them to another folder. * Hold down the Shift key to select multiple POMs at once and move them all. Delete Click on the Delete button to delete an entire folder or POMs within a folder. Note: If there are active POMs within the folder a pop up will come up asking you If you would like to delete the POMs or move them to the default folder. View Graded Sizes When Grading is applied to pattern, you will be able to view or hide different graded sizes within the Object Browser POM to improve visibility. When a pattern has grading applied the Graded sizes will automatically appear within the POM Object browser. Click on the size to hide it easily. Click on the size again to quickly reactivate it.

Title: Adjust Avatar Size
Content: List of Contents Open Avatar Editor Adjust Size Adjust Shape Open/Save AVS File Create an avatar with your own measurements. As CLO Avatar Editor is powered by thousands of real body scan data, even measurements not assigned by users automatically adjust to the most realistic body shape. Open Avatar Editor Open CLO Avatar File (.avt). Click the Main Menu Avatar Avatar Editor menu. Adjust Size Adjust the Avatar size and shape. Option Description Size Sets the overall body shape of the avatar. It is automatically adjusted based on actual body shape data according to the entered width and height measurements. Note: Click the link button to unlink and modify the width and height while keeping detailed measurements. Width Bust Set the overall body width based on the bust circumference. Under Bust Set the overall body width based on the under bust circumference. Set the type of Width to Under Bust, then adjusting the detailed measurements of Bust allows you to change the cup size while maintaining the overall body shape. Weight Set the overall body width by entering the weight. Height Total Height Enter the height measured from the ground to the head. Note: Since each person has a different head size, it is most accurate to create a overall body shape based on HPS Height or Inseam, rather than Total Height, which is less accurate and not recommended. HPS Height Enter the height measured from the ground to the neck. Inseam Enter the height measured from the ground to the crotch. Detailed Mesurements Adjust each specific circumference, height, and length by entering values directly. A small error may be generated when entering measurements, and the error appears when you click the Measures on the 3D Avatar. Movable Measure Select the Edit Measure Tool (Avatar) Click the Circumference Measure (black solid line) for Under Bust, Waist, High Hip, Low Hip, and Thigh Drag it to the desired position to set the baseline for resizing. Note: After changing the position, right-click on the Measure to reset it to its original position. Show Editable Measurements Select the Detailed Measurement to enter. The more Detailed Measurements you select, the more unnatural it may appear, as the measurements are not automatically adjusted and remain fixed to the entered values. Show All Measurements Check the measurements for all parts. Adjust Shape Adjust the Avatar size and shape. Option Description Shape Adjust the size of the avatar's hands, head, and crotch gap. For male avatars, Crotch Volume can also be adjusted. Achieve various breast shapes by adjusting the Breast Shape, Space and Height. Note: If you enter the Apex to Apex or HPS length and then adjust the Breast Space, discrepancies and distortions may occur in the entered length. Open/Save AVS File Click the Save or Open button in the Avatar Size Editor to manage the size data. Note: Avatar size files may not be fully compatible between the latest version (2024.1) and previous versions (2024.0 and below). It is recommended to use files matching the version.

Title: Grainline
Content: New in 2024.2 List of Content Grain Direction Link All Colorways Grain Orientation Grainline Lock Adjust the direction and orientation of the grainline, while also being able to lock Grainline properties and adjustments across all modes and features within CLO. Click the 2D pattern using the Transform Pattern or Edit Pattern tool in the 2D toolbar. Adjust the direction and orientation of the grainline in the Property Editor. Grain Direction The main angle/ degree for the pattern's placement on the fabric roll. 1) Click the text field. 2) Press the arrow keys on the keyboard to change the degree based on how the Grain Orientation is set up. Examples: Grain Orientation One way: The numbers will switch every 45 degrees. Grain Orientation Two Or Four Way: The numbers will switch every 90 Degrees. 3) Or enter a specific degree. Link All Colorways If there are multiple colorways within the project file checking this checkbox on will apply the grainline information to all colorways. If the checkbox is unchecked that means each colorway can be different. Note: This could be helpful if you want more control when entering production or if you are planning on having different fabrics for different colorways. Grain Orientation To decide how many different orientations/ directions the pattern can be placed on the fabric roll. Note:These options are very important for when moving into production and learning how much it would cost to produce the garment. This is also very important because based on the fabric you have applied certain the different orientations will change how much or how little stretch the garment has. One Way The pattern should only be placed in that one orientation that is dictated by the Grain Direction degree. Two Way The pattern can be placed in two different orientation. The degree dictated by the Grain Direction and the degree that is the direct opposite (180 degree from the original). Examples: 0 Degree Original: 180 Degree second option. 90 Degree Original: 270 Degree Second option. Four Way The pattern can be placed in four different orientations. The degree dictated by the Grain Direction and any other orientation that 90 degree from the original degree. Examples: 0 Degree Original: 90,180,270 other options. 45 Degree Original: 135,225,315 other options. Grainline Lock Checking this on will lock the grainline across all modes of CLO. Stopping any adjustments to the grainline when working with other tools or functions within CLO that can adjust the Grainline. Note: This locking is very helpful to keep continuity across all of CLO. The Print Layout mode and the Edit Texture tools will be the parts of CLO that are affected the most when checking this on or off.

Title: Set Fabric Materials
Content: List of Contents Fabric Properties Material Type Base Color Normal Map Displacement Map Opacity Reflection Express texture or pattern of the fabric. Fabric Properties Click a fabric in Fabric tab in Object Browser. Set the material properties in Property Editor. Material Type Set the appropriate CLO Material Type. Base Color Color Set the color of the fabric. Base Color Map Click the Open button to apply the Base Color Map. Note: Through the option of User Setting, you can convert the color profile of the image to sRGB when loading textures. Set the Recolor option as needed. Desaturate Desaturate the entire Base Color Map to remove color and convert it into grayscale or black and white. Color Switch Easily and quickly switch the color of solid fabric to a new one without losing the accuracy of the chosen color. Note: It is recommended to use the Texture Editor if the Base Color Map contains multiple colors, as it may not be switched properly. Please note that this Switch option is not synced with the Switch option in the Texture Editor. Normal Map Express uneven texture more realistically. When a texture is applied, Normal Map is generated by adjusting the Intensity. Or click the Open button to manually apply Normal Map image. Displacement Map Express thickness or bumpiness of fabrics or textures. You can find more detailed information here. Opacity Opacity Adjust the Opacity value to apply transparency to the fabric overall. Opacity Map Adjust level of transparency using a grayscale image map. Set the mode to determine whether the map's alpha value is encoded in the RGB channel or the alpha channel. Click the Open button to apply Opacity Map. Reflection Roughness Set whether to adjust the Roughness with the intensity value or apply it as a specific map. Adjust the values to express fabric gloss. Check the Invert option to make the shiny parts becomes dull and vice versa when using the map. Reflection Adjust the intensity value to express fabric reflection. Metalness Adjust the value to apply metallics to the fabric overall. Or click the Open button to partially apply metallics using a grayscale image. * The white parts of the map appear metallic. Note: When working with Metalness Map, control Roughness Intensity and Reflection Intensity level that are suitable for the metallic texture. (e.g. Roughness Intensity 10, Reflection Intensity 90) For the non-metallic areas (matte), assign the same metalness map to Roughness Map, and turn on Invert. Note: When clicking the Back/Side tab and turning off 'Use Same Material as Front' option, you can apply different materials to the back and side of the pattern and also you can set 'Use Same Color as Front' option.

Title: Nest Patterns
Content: List of Contents Switch Mode Nest Pattern Nest Settings Reset Default Arrangement Snapshot Efficiently layout patterns and check fabric consumption to use the least amount of fabric. Switch Mode Switch to Print Layout mode on the top-right corner of CLO. Nest Patterns Click the Nest Pattern tool in the toolbar. Patterns are efficiently placed on the fabric and the calculated value is displayed. Click the Stop Nesting tool in the toolbar. Pattern Nesting will stop. Note: Directly click the pattern Drag it within the set fabric width to place it or place the pattern using Align and Distribute. Instead of waiting for nesting to complete, stop directly at any point in time to place patterns to save nesting time. The number of calculations varies depending on the number of patterns. Higher counts give optimal arrangement results, but larger numbers of patterns require more calculations and take more time. Moving one space of the progress bar means that once the calculation has been completed. Nest Settings Click the Nest Setting tool in the toolbar. Nesting Options appear in the Property Editor. Set each property. Menu Description Nesting Number of Garment Nest grading patterns on the fabric for mass production. By clicking the Select Grading button, manually set the size and quantity(amount) of the grading patterns to be nested. Note: Different colors can be displayed for each grading size on the fabric and you can check the size names. (ver 7.2) Display grading colors: 2D Pattern Display Show Grading Random Color icon Display grading names: 2D Information Display Show Grading Size icon Group Each Sizes Click the Group Each Sizes option to nest patterns by grouping the graded sizes separately. Colorway Nest patterns of all colorways on the fabric or click Select Colorway on the right to place only the selected colorway on the fabric. Grain Direction 1-way Place the pattern in one orientation along the original grain direction 2-way Place the pattern in the opposite orientation that is 180 degrees from the original orientation to achieve optimized results. 4-way Place the pattern in four different orientations that are each 90 degrees from the original orientation to achieve optimized results. Buffer Spacing Set the spacing between patterns. Pattern Dimension Actual Place the pattern in its actual size. Shrinkage /Growth Place the pattern with the shrinkage rate applied. Information Unit Set the units. Fabric Width Adjust the width of the fabric. Length Check the total length of the fabric on which the pattern is placed. Marker Length (ver 7.2) Set the length of the fabric manually to nest the pattern only up to the length of the set fabric. Efficiency Consumption Based on 100% of the total fabric, the fabric area consumed for the pattern is calculated as % Remnant The remainder after subtracting the area consumed by the pattern is calculated as a %. Area Pattern Placed Check the pattern area placed on the fabric. Remnant Check the remaining area where no pattern is placed. Reset Default Arrangement Click the Reset Default Arrangement tool in the toolbar. Patterns are reset to the initial arrangement state. Snapshot Click the Snapshot tool in the toolbar. 2D Snapshot pop-up window appears. By Setting the option, the state of the patterns placed on the fabric is saved as an image. Note: Patterns and Internal Shapes with adhesion/bonding are classified separately in the Bond tab.

Title: Seam Taping
Content: Reinforce edges of Patterns to withstand from drooping down by gravity when Simulating. Click on the Seam Taping tool on the 2D toolbar. Select a segment Pattern to reinforce, or Click-and-drag also allows applying seam tapes. Activate the Simulate. The seam tape is now being applied to the selected segment and being reinforced. Provide the options for seam tape extension. Click on the segment with seam tape applied with Seam Taping tool. Set the Extend option in the Property Editor. None Seam tape does not extend. To Outline Extend to the pattern outline. To Seam Taping Extend to another seam tape area of the intersected line. * The arrow highlighted on the segment indicates the direction from start to end. Note: When extending a seam tape to another seam taping, please make sure there is an intersected seam tape for reference. If you apply Seam Taping Extend in the lower version (before ver 2024.2), both Start and End are assigned as To Outline in the higher version.

Title: Set Color Theme
Content: New in CLO 2024.2. Set the theme to Dark or Light based on your preference and environment. Dark theme uses a dark background for the user interface, reducing eye strain and glare, especially in low-light environments. It helps to keep the overall brightness of the screen lower, which can be more comfortable during prolonged use. Light theme, on the other hand, features a bright background that provides a clean and crisp appearance, improving readability in well-lit environments. Click on the Setting User Settings in the menu bar. Set the theme under User Interface &gt Appearance. Restart CLO to apply the theme.

Title: Colorway (ver 2024.1)
Content: List of Contents Open and Update Add Edit Set Option View Mode Snapshot A garment file can be applied in various colors. Open and Update Click the Main Menu Production Colorway. After editing and adjusting the 3D view, click the Update button at the top left of the Colorway Editor. Add Add (Default) Click the 'Add' button at the top-right corner in Colorway Editor. By default, a colorway is added based on the selected colorway, allowing only the material properties such as color and texture to be changed. Therefore, a single item (fabric, graphic, trims, etc.) will have different materials for each colorway, and this can be confirmed in the object browser. Note: Even if the Colorway Editor window is closed, you can check the variations for each colorway in the object browser, and you can show or hide them with the 'Show All Colorways' option in the top left corner. Add as Custom Settings For various colorways, you can directly set the variation application range for each item. Refer to the example below and set it at once in the colorway addition step, and easily edit and manage it. Click the 'Add as Custom Settings' button at the top-right corner in Colorway Editor. A list of items for the selected colorway appears in the Add Colorway window. Directly set the variation application range for each item of the colorway to be added. Option Description Materials Based on the item of the selected colorway, only material properties such as color and texture can be changed. The same applies as for additional (default) results. Example) If the physical properties of the fabric and the shape of the button are the same but only the color is different All Properties Items in the selected colorway are automatically copied and applied as new items, allowing all properties to be changed differently. Example) If it is a completely different fabric or the shape of the button is different. Link It can be used as the same item as the selected colorway without changing its properties. This option is applied simultaneously when two items are linked to each other and their properties are changed. Example) When the same fabric and graphics (logo) are used in all colorways Edit Change Properties Select the thumbnail of the item you want to change in the Colorway Editor window, or select the item in the object browser. The properties of the item appear in the property editor. Change material properties. Properties other than material can be changed by directly selecting the corresponding item in the object browser. Note: After selecting a graphic with Transform Graphic tool, uncheck the 'Property Editor &gt Link All Colorways &gt Angle or Position' option to rotate or position the graphic differently for each colorway. Assign Items Apply the files of each item (fabric, graphics, subsidiary materials, etc.) directly to the pattern by dragging and dropping them. The item applied to all colorways of the pattern will be replaced at once, and different materials can be applied to each colorway. Press the Ctrl key on the keyboard while dragging. A single item is linked and applied to all colorways of the pattern.. Note: When you drag and drop the thumbnail of each item in the Colorway Editor window, it can only be applied to the item of that colorway, not all colorways. You can easily and quickly choose whether to apply it to the current colorway only or to all colorways when assigning an item from the Object Browser. Drag and drop the Fabric from Object Browser to the 3D garment. In the Assign to Colorway window, specify how an item will be assigned to the colorway by default. * This window will appear only the first time. Even with a default setting, the option can still be changed by pressing the Ctrl key while dragging and dropping afterward. You can easily assign items directly to the Colorway Editor. Drag and drop the items from Object Browser, Library or your computer onto the thumbnail in Colorway Editor. Set Option Right-click on each colorway or each item's thumbnail in a colorway to set the desired options. Option Description Colorway Delete Delete the colorway. Rename Change the name of the colorway. Item Unlink All Colorways Unlink the linked item so that it can have different materials applied to each colorway or apply different properties altogether. Select All with Same Color The same color within the colorway is automatically selected. You can quickly hide multiple graphics at once. Right-click on the Graphic thumbnail in the Colorway Editor. Click the Hide Other Graphics menu to hide all other graphics that use the same item as the selected graphic. View Mode Click the Show Details button at the bottom-right corner. Colorway window switches to "Viewer Mode" where you can see the colorway thumbnails only. Size thumbnails by controlling the scroll bar at the bottom-left corner, or arrange the thumbnails in single or multiple lines by clicking the arrangement button. Snapshot Click on the Save Image button at the left-top corner. Select either 3D Window (Colorway Thumbnail) or Colorway Editor, then click OK. Save the image after choosing the file extension, the saving path and file name. Note: If you save the garment with colorway as a project file in version 2024.1, it may not be compatible properly with lower versions (2024.0, 7.3). Therefore, if necessary, it is recommended to separately save the project file for colorway compatibility through the 'Main Menu &gt File &gt Save As &gt Project (with Other Files) menu' option.

Title: Copy/Paste/Replace
Content: List of Contents Copy and Paste Replace Depending on the user's needs, copy and paste patterns or replace them only in the form of a specific pattern while maintaining the original properties. Copy and Paste Click the Transform Pattern or Edit Pattern tool on the 2D toolbar. Right-click on the pattern or Internal line to be copied. Click the Copy (Ctrl+C) menu. Right-click on the 2D background and click the Paste (Ctrl+V) menu. Press the Shift key to place it on a vertical/horizontal/45 line or freely click anywhere you want. Note: Right-clicking during paste allows you to enter values for Interval/Number of Shapes/Position (Internal Line). Patterns can be copied and pasted even between multi-run CLO programs. Replace Right-click on the original pattern to be replaced. Click the Replace menu. The pattern is replaced with the copied pattern's segment point locations, curves, notches, baselines, pattern names, and grading information. Sewing lines, Internal shapes, Graphics, Fabrics, Topstitching, Puckering, and buttons are maintained as the properties of the original pattern. Note: Pattern replacement is only possible if the number of Segment points is the same. Even if the old and new patterns have different segment points, you can easily replace them. Right-click on the original pattern, internal line, internal shape, baseline, or baseline shape to be replaced. Click Replaced by menu. The original pattern or line is replaced with the new one's segment point locations, curves, notches, baselines, pattern names, and grading information. Sewing lines, Internal shapes, Graphics, Fabrics, Topstitching, Puckering, and buttons are maintained as the properties of the original pattern. Select the new pattern, internal line, internal shape, baseline, or baseline shape. When the number of segment points is the same, the replacement process will be completed automatically. Click and match the Segment point from the original pattern to the new pattern. When the number of segment points differs, the Segment point matching action is required. After matching enough Segment points, the replacement process will be completed automatically. Press the Enter key to complete if enough core points have been matched or if there are no more points to match. Note: If both the original and new patterns are half-symmetry, their center points will automatically align. For unclosed internal shapes or baseline shapes, their endpoints are automatically matched. Press the Delete to cancel the last step, or Press the Esc key to cancel all actions

Title: Linked Editing
Content: List of Contents Set Linked Editing Remove Linked Editing You can set linked editing to edit the pattern more quickly and efficiently. Set Linked Editing Symmetric Pattern Right-click on the pattern to clone it symmetrically with Transform Pattern tool. Click on 'Clone Pattern with Linked Editing Symmetric Pattern (with Sewing)/Symmetric Pattern' menu. Click on the 2D window to arragne the clone. Instance Pattern Right-click on the pattern to clone it as an instance with Transform Pattern tool. Click on 'Clone Pattern with Linked Editing Instance Pattern' menu. Click on the 2D window to arrange the clone, or right-click on the 2D window while arranging to set the number of shapes and define the interval. Note: Right-click on both patterns that are not linked and select the 'Apply Linked Editing' menu to apply linked editing without cloning. Remove Linked Editing Right-click on the pattern to remove linked editing with Transform Pattern tool. Click on the 'Remove Linked Eidting' menu. Linked editing can be removed only for the internal lines within a pattern, while keeping linked editing for the overall pattern.

Title: Freeze/Unfreeze
Content: Objective Use this function to fasten patterns like solid objects. Deactivated patterns do not collide during simulation, however, frozen patterns do (they maintain collision). Therefore, it is better to use for draping multiple layered garments. For instance, draping and freezing inner garments first, then draping outerwear above helps avoid occasional instabilities. Location 3D Toolbar Select/Move 2D Toolbar Transform Pattern Operation Select the tool/menu indicated above. Right-click on the 3D or 2D pattern and click Freeze/Unfreeze. The pattern selected is frozen/unfrozen. Note: Right-click in the empty space of the 3D window and hover over Show/Hide Color, then click Show Freeze to show or hide the color applied during freeze. (ver 6.1)

Title: Grading Review
Content: List of Contents Generate Data for Review Open Layout Setting Full Screen Save Image All Grading Sizes of Garments and Avatars can be compared on one screen. Grading Review is activated based on the simulated results for each grading size. Generate Data for Review Click the Pair Avatar tab and click the Update after creating and editing the grading. The 3D window's avatar is basically applied to all sizes. If there are two or more size groups, they are combined based on the base size. Change the avatar for each grading size as needed. Click the checkbox to the right of each size item and simulate. The simulation result of the garment of the size on the avatar is automatically saved. After simulation for each size, if the mesh of the pattern is changed due to work such as pattern correction, simulation must be performed again. Open Click the Main Menu Production Grading Review. If re-simulation is required, click the simulation at the top left of each size. Move, zoom and rotate the view of the 3D window. Click the icon at the top to set the rendering status of the garment and avatar. Show or hide the Pressure map in the Grading Review. Click and hold the Fit Maps tool for more than 2 seconds, then click the Pressure Map. Re-simulate to get the result. Layout Setting Enter the width and height directly to adjust the size of each 3D window. Click theLayout to set the 3D window layout. Options Description Wrap The 3D windows will be wrapped and aligned according to the width of the Grading Review window Horizontal Align the 3D windows horizontally. Vertical Align the 3D windows vertically. Panoramic All grading sizes can be checked and compared at one in a single 3D window. Rotation Each grading size rotates on the X-axis. Distance The Space for each grading size is adjusted Click the Reset Layout to return to the initial layout. Full Screen Click theFull Screen. Press the ESC key on your keyboard to exit Full Screen. Save Image Click the Save and specify a name and path. Check the option to save Transparent Background and Separate Images and click the 'Save'. Note: Right-click on the screen if you click the Hide Grading Size, the hidden size disappears in the 3D window.

Title: Trim Grading
Content: New in 2024.2 Apply grading rules to Trims added to Patterns. Open trim to Pattern. Create grading sizes or apply existing grading sizes. Select the trim in the 2D window using the Grading tool in the 2D toolbar. Use the arrow keys or configure options as needed to edit grading rules. * Base Size cannot be edited. Note: Grading rules applied to the trim only affect trim placement, not size.

Title: How to Use Pins
Content: List of Contents Create Pin Hide/Show Pin Delete Pin Affix specific portions of the garment and utilize pins similarly to the Freeze function. It is also convenient when turning/flipping over collars, lapels, or cuffs. Create Pin Click while pressing W on the keyboard with Select/Move tool on the 3D toolbar. OR Click and hold the Select Mesh tool for more than 2 seconds, then click the Pin (Box) or Pin (Lasso) tool. The mesh of all pattern pieces will be shown in red. Follow the indicated guideline below: Vertex Click on a vertex, which is any point in the mesh where edges meet. When hovering above, a blue dot will appear. Area Click on the desired area on the garment click and drag to select the area. Segment Double-click on a pattern outline in either the 3D or 2D window to create pins on a segment. When creating pins on the pattern in the 2D window, they are generated on adjacent segment vertices when the angle difference is less than 20. Pattern Double-click on a pattern in either the 3D or 2D window to create pins all across its entire surface. Internal Line Use the same procedure as above to create pins on specific internal lines and shapes. Click and drag, or use the gizmo to move the pinned mesh as desired in the 3D window. Note: Click and drag on the 2D pattern while holding Shift+Ctrl (Windows) / Shift+Cmmd (Mac) on the keyboard to create additional pinned areas. Adversely, click and drag on the 2D pattern while holding Ctrl (Windows) / Cmmd (Mac) on the keyboard to remove pins from existing pinned areas. Holding Shift and then clicking and dragging will remove pins where there were some and add where there were none. The created pin can also be selected in the 2D Window. (ver 7.3 ) You can quickly duplicate pins and its position to the symmetric side/pattern in one click. Right-click on the pin on a symmetric pattern. In the menu that appears, click on Duplicate to Symmetric Patterns. Note: Once duplicated, any position changes you make will not dynamically affect the symmetric sides/patterns. Hide/Show Pin Hover over the Garment Display in the 3D or 2D window for more than 2 seconds, then click the Show Pins icon. You can hide pins in Print Layout mode as needed. Delete Pin Right-click on the pin. In the menu that appears, click Delete Selected Pin / Delete All Pins. While on the Select/Move tool, selecting a created pin while holding W key on keyboard also deletes the pin.

Title: CLO Fabric Creator
Content: List of Contents Open Create Fabric Set Options Apply and Save Simply enter your Fabric Type, Composition and Density to quickly create new accurate fabrics within CLO. Open Right-click on the fabric item in Fabric tab in Object browser, then select the Fabric Creator menu. It can also work in Main Menu Editor Fabric Creator Menu, and if it work in this way, the created fabric is addded as a new fabric Create Fabric Enter the Name, Supplier, and Owner of the fabric. When selecting the Fabric Type and entering the Composition, the physical properties of the fabric are applied according to the information set and will be previewed. Switch tap to check and modify the physical properties of the fabric as needed. Set the Material of the fabric it created, or click the Use CLO Texture Presets option to enable and apply the CLO default textures based on the fabric type. The Composition can be customized based on the selected Fabric Type. Select the Fabric Type Click on the Select menu and then choose the compositions to customize. * Basic refers to the primary composition used for the selected fabric type, while Additional refers to compositions that can be combined as extras. When entering the composition, the physical properties of the fabric are applied according to the information set and will be previewed. Set Options Model Set the shape to preview the fabric (Cylinder-Circle /Squar, Cape) in the upper left corner of the Fabric Creator window. View Set the preview to a specified view, or manually adjust to set the desired view in the upper right corner of the fabric Creator window. Note: Click the Lock button to lock the view adjusted. Apply and Save After the fabric is created, click the Apply and Apply &amp Close buttons at the bottom. If the fabric is applied in the 3D garment, the results can be checked right away. The Fabric Creator window is closed simultaneously as it is applied as the property of the fabric. Or, click the Save button to save the created fabric as a file. (ZFAB).

Title: Realistic Knitwear Designer
Content: Create realistic knitwear with a variety of stitchings. Click the Fabric in Fabric tab in Object Browser, and then Change the Material Type to Knitwear in Property Editor. Adjust each detail property to express the desired knitwear. Properties Description Stitching Set the knit's Stitching type. Yarn Thickness Set the thickness of the yarn. Gauge Gauge refers to the number of knitting stitches within an inch. This means you can control the size of a stitch in the knit fabric: Higher values represent denser, thinner knits, and lower values represent thicker knits. Knit Direction Adjust the Knit Direction. Ply Amount Set the number of threads for plying. Ply Randomization (Melange) Plying is randomly blended to create a natural melange effect. Randomization Factor Adjust the density of the plying. Higher values result in a denser appearance. Seed Position Adjust the position of the plying. Yarn Variance Irreqularity Scale Adjust how much the yarn randomly moves. Frequency Adjust how often the yarn direction changes. Pilling Length (mm) Adjust how short or long the fluff can get. Higher values result in a longer pilling appearance. Thickness Adjust how thick the fluff can get. Higher values result in a thicker pilling appearance. Frequency Adjust how often the fluff appears. Generate Seams Additional yarn is created along the seam lines and pattern outlines. If the seams of the knitwear pattern are unnatural, adjust the option to make them look natural. Ply Normal Map Apply the normal map to the plying to express the three-dimensional effect of the yarn. Ply Color Set the color for each yarn in the plying. Note: It may affect performance and speed when applying knitwear, and you can turn off the Garment Rendering Style in 3D window Show Knitwear during other operations to work at the same speed as before. To optimize the knitwear mesh in the invisible camera area of the final rendered image, apply the settings in Render Properties Mesh Optimization.

Title: OBJ Trim
Content: List of Contents Open/Ad Glue Set Properties Set Options Manage Trim as a style in the Object Browser. Open/Add Click the button in the Trim tab in the Object Browser. Import an OBJ file as a Trim, or open the Trim (TRM) file. Drag and Drop the Trim Style to the 3D window from the Object Browser. Glue Click on the Trim in 3D window with Select/Move tool. Click the Glue button next to the Gizmo, then click on the desired location. Click the Simulate tool. Set Properties Set the trim style properties or options by clicking the trim style in the Object Browser. Information Enter the information of trim Specification Scale Scale trim with X, Y, and Z-axis. Note: You can directly scale the trim using the gizmo by clicking the scale button next to the gizmo in 3D window. Axis Enter the desired value for each axis. Lock Aspect Ratio Toggle this option on to adjust a trim while maintaining its x, y, and z ratio. Weight Set the weight of trim. The entered value of weight is reflected in the simulation. Material Set the Material. Or set the trim properties individually by clicking on the trim in 3D window. Name If each part(meshes) of the OBJ trim is composed of two or more parts, you can set the name for each part individually. Collision Set whether you turn the Collision on or off. It only enables or disables the Collision of detached trim. Collision Thickness Set the Collision Thickness with a garment. The higher the value is, the farther the distance with a garment is in the simulation. Material Partially set the material of trim Set Options Right- click on the trim in the 3D window to set the options. Select All Trims Select all trims in the 3D Window. Delete Delete selected trims. Copy/ Paste Copy and paste the selected trims. Duplicate to Symmerty Pattern Duplicate the selected trims to the symmetry pattern. Unglue The attatched trim is being detached from the Pattern. Hide Trim/Show All Trims Hide/Show all trims. Simulate trim to achieve realistic movement and seamless, stable interaction with 3D garments. Note: Trim simulation is available only for unglued trims, which are set to Activate by default with both simulation and collision applied. Arrange the trim in the desired position on the 3D garment in the 3D window, then click the Simulate tool. If you want to activate only collision without simulation, right-click on the trim and click the Freeze menu. Or, if you want to deactivate both collision and simulation, and click the Deactivate menu.

Title: Simulation
Content: Use this function to apply gravity and drape 3D garment in the 3D window. Pressing the Simulate button causes all Garment Patterns to fall towards the floor, and drape onto Avatars and similar objects that are in the way. When seamlines are set between Garment Patterns, the fabric drapes and falls while the set seamlines are sewn. Click on the Simulate tool in the 3D toolbar. Click and hold the Simulate tool for more than 2 seconds to change the simulation options. Option Description Fast (GPU) The Simulation speed improves depending on the computer's graphic card specification. * As the collision is calculated with a different algorithm when using GPU for simulation, the simulation result created with CPU and GPU are different. Please learn more in detail from the FAQ linked below: * This feature is only available on Windows computers with an NVIDIA GeForce GTX 960 or higher graphics card. Normal (Default) The Garment simulation is more efficiently with faster speed. Fabric properties are accurately calculated in Normal (Default) Simulation setting as well. Animation (Stable) Garment simulation is more defined but the simulation speed may decrease. Fitting (Accurate Fabric) Garment simulation is more defined and fabric stretch is expressed more realistically. GPU simulation with the same level of accuracy and collision handling as CPU simulation in all modes (Normal, Animation and Fitting). Note: Currently GPU simulation is not possible within Soft Body, Trim and Knitwear Simulation.

Title: Register Hair/Shoes
Content: OBJ production Register Objective Register the Avatar's Hair/Shoes as an accessory file(ZACS). Location Main menu Avatar Register Hair/Shoes Operation OBJ production When making OBJ in other 3D programs(Maya, 3ds Max, etc.), please follow the requirements below. Set the work environment of the 3D program. (Axis: Y-Up, Unit: Millimeter) Create a hair/shoes OBJ according to the avatar file. Avatar Prepare an avatar suitable for the hair/shoes to be registered. CLO's default avatar or user avatar can be used. Mesh For the sharp angular expression, add an edge to the mesh to be reliably simulated in the CLO. Dummy Mesh For complex areas (shoelaces, heels, etc.) where the faces come into contact, wrap in a transparent and flat dummy mesh. Make the spacing between dummy meshes smaller and more consistent than shoe meshes. Meah Name Hair hair Shoes (shoes_r, shoes_l) Materials Apply separately various materials(leather, metal, plastic, etc.) Even if the heel is the same material, it must be applied separately and the order must be at the bottom. Set the transform properties. (Translate/ Rotation: All axes 0, Scale: All axes 1) Export to FBX file. Register Open the avatar file for the hair/shoes to be registered. Note: It is recommended to open additionally the hair/shoes file(FBX) to be registered and check that the position with the avatar is correct. Select the tool/menu indicated. The Hair/Shoes registration window appears. After setting the following options, click the Create button. Menu Description Hair/Shoes Select the type of hair, shoes and glasses &amp earrings(ver 7.1). File Path (FBX) Select the path of the hair and shoe files to be registered. Thumbnail Add a thumbnail image to be displayed in the library window. The save file window appears. Set the file name and path. It is saved as a hair/shoes file(ZACS). Trouble-Shooting Make sure the mesh layer noted below has the correct nomenclature in Blender. The other names do not matter. Otherwise, you may encounter an error message that the name is wrong.

Title: Convert to Curve Point
Content: Easily convert Segment Points on the patterns to Curve Points, or Curve Points to Segment Points Right-click on the segment point with Edit Pattern tool or on the curve point with Edit Curve Point tool. Click the Convert to Curve Point. Option Description Maintain Curve Convert selected points by automatically adding curve points to maintain the curvature. If the segment is already smooth enough, no curved points will added. Convert Only Convert selected points without adding curve points. The segment result may be affected slightly. Note: Clicking while holding down the Shift key on the keyboard allows for multiple selections.

Title: Express Fur
Content: List of Contents Apply Fur Fur Parameters Fur Gradation Color Fur Base Fur Maps Fur Gravity Fur Curl Fur Variance Express coat, fur coat, fleece and more realistically by visualizing different shaped and color fur. Apply Fur Change the Material Type to the Fur. * Fur can only be previewed in the Interactive Render. Select one of the presets to express Fox, Mink, Angora, Sherpa and more. Fur Parameters Set the fur parameters. Option Description Melanin Co nfigure saturation of the fur's original color. Hi ghe r the Melanin value is, saturated the color is. On the other hand, lower the value is, light the color is. PheoMelanin Configure how reddish the fur is. Higher the PheoMelanin value is, redder the fur is. PheoMelanin value is applied in proportion to Melanin value, PheoMelanin value is not counted when the Melanin value is 0. Glossiness Configure shininess of the fur. When the light is applied to the fur, shinier it is with a higher value. Glossiness Boost Express coated fur. Glossiness adjusts intrinsic shininess of the fur whereas Glossiness Boost expresses the shininess from the fur finishing, like wax or coating. Higher the Glossiness Boost value is, the stronger the fur finishing effect is. Softness Express smoothness of the fur. Higher the Softness value is, smoother the fur is. On the other hand, the lower the value is, rougher the fur is. Fur Gradation Color Apply the Fur Gradation Color by clicking the check box and set the gradation properties. Option Description Fur Gradation Color Color Select the mid and the tip color of the gradation. Position Adjust the length of the fur where Mid and Tip Color is applied. Interpolation Naturally blend the borders of tip, mid, and root colors. Fur Base Set the Base properties. Option Description Length Configure the length of the fur. Higher the value is, longer the fur is. Length: 50 Length: 10 Thickness Configure the thickness of a single thread of the fur. Higher the value is, thicker the fur is. Thickness: 10 Thickness: 0.20 Bend Configure the bending strength of the fur. Higher the value is, more affected by the gravity and bends more. Bend: 1.00 Bend: 0.20 Taper Differentiate the thickness of the fur between its root and the end. Higher the value is, thinner the fur becomes toward the end. On the other hand, lower the value is, similar the thickness is between the root and the end. Taper : 1.00 (Thickness: 2.00) Taper : 0.00 (Thickness:2.00) Density Configure how fur are closely placed. Higher the value is, more dense the fur is. On the other hand, lower the value is, more scattered the fur is. Density: 1.00 Density: 0.20 Segments Configure how many sections a single thread of fur is divided into.When the fur is long and has higher Bending value, the fur must have higher Segments value to express the Bending smoothly and realistically. However, for the short and straight fur, the Segments value is not as significant. Fur Maps Use Base Maps to express different length, thickness, and density within a single Pattern. 0 is multiplied to the Length, Thickness, and Density values when a Map is black. On the other hand, 1 is multiplied to the Length, Thickness, and Density values when a Map is white. For example: You can easily generate the realistic Fur Cluster by controlling the length and bend direction. Open Fur Cluster Generator by clicking the button. Generate the Fur Cluster. Properties Description Length Cropping Map Use the Cropping Map to apply different length within a single pattern. Mode As a cropping map is grayscale, the length is determined based on the level of darkness (RGB) or the transparency (Alpha). Transparent and black areas have Lowest Length, while opaque and white areas have Highest Length. Level Adjust intensity of gray tones. Increasing the value makes the cropping effect more obvious. Low/High Length Adjust the shortest or longest fur length. Trimming Intensity Trim the length from the edge to the center of the fur cluster. Higher intensity increases the difference in fur length from the edge to the center to create a sharper fur. Random Higher Random makes the clumps irregular, while lower Random makes the clumps consistent. Bend Direction Cluster Intensity Adjusts the intensity of the fur bending in each direction. Higher intensity makes the fur clump more pronounced and dimensional. Pores Density Adjust the pores density of the fur cluster. Higher density makes the clumps smaller and tighter, while lower density makes the clumps larger and more spread out. Direction/ Intensity Random Adjust whether the bend direction is consistent or irregular. Detail Cluster The clumping of smaller sub-units within the cluster can be adjusted in the same way as the cluster. Relax Adjust the intensity of clumping in detail clusters while keeping each direction intact. Higher Relax makes the clumps loosen smoothly, as if gently combed out. Fur Gravity Set the Gravity properties. Option Description Force Apply the force of gravity. Vector Manually apply the Gravity value to each axis. Fur Curl Set the Curl properties. Option Description Radius Configure the size of the curl.Higher the value is, larger the curl is. On the other hand, lower the value is, smaller the curl is. Radius : 5.00 (Number: 5.00) Radius : 1.00 (Number:5.00) Number Configure the number of the curls. Higher the value is, more curls the fur has. On the other hand, lower the value is, less curls the fur has. Number : 5.00 (Radius: 5.00) Number : 0.00 (Radius: 5.00) Fur Variance Set the Variance properties. Option Description Length Express uniformed or irregular fur length.Higher the value is, irregular the fur length is. On the other hand, lower the value is, uniform the length is. Thickness Express uniformed or irregular fur thickness.Higher the value is, irregular the fur thickness is. On the other hand, lower the value is, uniform the thickness is. Direction Express uniformed or irregular fur bending direction.Higher the value is, irregular the fur bending direction is. On the other hand, lower the value is, uniform the bending direction is. Gravity Express uniformed or irregular gravity effect. Higher the value is, irregular the gravity effect is. On the other hand, lower the value is, uniform the gravity effect is. Gravity value can only be applied when the Bending value is not 0.
